# Microsoft Azure Monitor management client library for .NET

Microsoft Azure Monitor helps you maximize the availability and performance of your applications and services. It delivers a comprehensive solution for collecting, analyzing, and acting on telemetry from your cloud and on-premises environments.

This library supports managing Microsoft Azure Monitor resources.

This library follows the [new Azure SDK guidelines](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/general_introduction.html), and provides many core capabilities:

    - Support MSAL.NET, Azure.Identity is out of box for supporting MSAL.NET.
    - Support [OpenTelemetry](https://opentelemetry.io/) for distributed tracing.
    - HTTP pipeline with custom policies.
    - Better error-handling.
    - Support uniform telemetry across all languages.

## Getting started 

### Install the package

Install the Microsoft Azure Monitor management library for .NET with [NuGet](https://www.nuget.org/):

```dotnetcli
dotnet add package Azure.ResourceManager.Monitor
```

### Prerequisites

* You must have an [Microsoft Azure subscription](https://azure.microsoft.com/free/dotnet/).

### Authenticate the Client

To create an authenticated client and start interacting with Microsoft Azure resources, see the [quickstart guide here](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/doc/dev/mgmt_quickstart.md).

## Key concepts

Key concepts of the Microsoft Azure SDK for .NET can be found [here](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/dotnet_introduction.html).

## Documentation

Documentation is available to help you learn how to use this package:

- [Quickstart](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/doc/dev/mgmt_quickstart.md).
- [API References](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/?view=azure-dotnet).
- [Authentication](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/sdk/identity/Azure.Identity/README.md).

## Examples

Code samples for using the management library for .NET can be found in the following locations
- [.NET Management Library Code Samples](https://aka.ms/azuresdk-net-mgmt-samples)

## Troubleshooting

-   File an issue via [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/issues).
-   Check [previous questions](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/azure+.net) or ask new ones on Stack Overflow using Azure and .NET tags.

## Next steps

For more information about Microsoft Azure SDK, see [this website](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/).

## Contributing

For details on contributing to this repository, see the [contributing
guide][cg].

This project welcomes contributions and suggestions. Most contributions
require you to agree to a Contributor License Agreement (CLA) declaring
that you have the right to, and actually do, grant us the rights to use
your contribution. For details, visit <https://cla.microsoft.com>.

When you submit a pull request, a CLA-bot will automatically determine
whether you need to provide a CLA and decorate the PR appropriately
(for example, label, comment). Follow the instructions provided by the
bot. You'll only need to do this action once across all repositories
using our CLA.

This project has adopted the [Microsoft Open Source Code of Conduct][coc]. For
more information, see the [Code of Conduct FAQ][coc_faq] or contact
<opencode@microsoft.com> with any other questions or comments.

proposals.subtype: Tracked-resource model contract and location constructor
proposals.explanation: ActivityLogAlertData explicitly derives from TrackedResourceData and supplies a public AzureLocation constructor forwarding location to the base. This establishes the displayed base-type/construction contract without proving the different historical or generated base type asserted in comments.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The explicit inheritance clause and constructor are handwritten in src/Customization/Compatibility outside Generated.

proposals.subtype: Condition-list facade with nested condition replacement
proposals.explanation: ConditionAllOf initializes missing Properties with AlertRuleProperties in both accessors. The getter returns Properties.ConditionAllOf, while the setter replaces Properties.Condition with new AlertRuleAllOfCondition(value), rather than directly assigning the getter's nested list.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The complete state-initializing getter/setter is implemented in the handwritten compatibility partial.

proposals.subtype: Obsolete collection facade with unsupported operations and enumeration
proposals.explanation: The hidden obsolete AlertRuleCollection declares an ArmCollection with sync/async enumeration and a protected mocking constructor. Its Get, GetAll, Exists, GetIfExists and CreateOrUpdate pairs and all three enumeration implementations immediately throw NotSupportedException. These members form one uniformly retired collection facade, not functioning paging, existence checks or LRO behavior.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The full non-generated obsolete type, constructor and uniform throwing implementations are supplied in the compatibility folder.

proposals.subtype: Obsolete model surface with unsupported construction and serialization
proposals.explanation: AlertRuleData is a hidden obsolete TrackedResourceData subclass retaining its listed auto-properties. Its location/name/enabled/condition constructor calls the base then throws NotSupportedException; JsonModelWriteCore and the JSON/persistence read/write methods also throw, while GetFormatFromOptions returns "J". The retained type surface does not provide a working model codec.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The entire placeholder model and explicit interface implementations are manually supplied outside Generated.

proposals.subtype: Obsolete resource facade with unsupported operations
proposals.explanation: The hidden obsolete AlertRuleResource retains its resource-type constant, protected constructor and uninitialized get-only Data/HasData properties. Identifier creation, Get, tag mutation, incident reads/lists, Delete and both BinaryData/AlertRulePatch Update pairs immediately throw NotSupportedException. JSON/persistence read/write methods likewise throw except GetFormatFromOptions returning "J". This is one retired resource facade, not implemented service operations, paging, polling or JSON conversion.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The complete obsolete ArmResource implementation is handwritten under src/Customization/Compatibility, with directly visible unsupported method bodies.

proposals.subtype: Obsolete factory overload adapting legacy aggregation arguments
proposals.explanation: A signature-specific suppression is paired with a hidden obsolete MonitorMetricDefinition factory. A non-null legacy supported-aggregation sequence is converted item by item through FromLegacyAggregationType into a new List<MonitorMetricAggregationType>; null remains null. The primary aggregation argument is also passed through that helper before forwarding to a same-name factory overload. Neither the helper's mapping nor the destination body is captured.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The active suppression and full handwritten adapting overload are supplied in the compatibility factory partial.

proposals.subtype: Obsolete alert-rule output factory throwing unsupported
proposals.explanation: The public AlertRuleData factory retains the displayed resource metadata, rule settings, action and action-list parameters but is hidden and obsolete and immediately throws NotSupportedException rather than constructing a model.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The obsolete metadata and complete throwing factory implementation are handwritten outside Generated.

proposals.subtype: Obsolete diagnostic-category model factory throwing unsupported
proposals.explanation: DiagnosticSettingsCategoryData remains a hidden obsolete public factory accepting resource metadata, category type and category groups; its implementation immediately throws NotSupportedException.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: This named output-model factory is manually implemented in the non-generated compatibility partial.

proposals.subtype: Obsolete diagnostic-setting model factory throwing unsupported
proposals.explanation: The hidden obsolete DiagnosticSettingData factory retains its resource, destination, metrics and logs arguments but immediately throws NotSupportedException. No destination selection or serialization behavior is implemented by this body.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: A concrete unsupported factory body is handwritten outside Generated, independently of comments about the current specification.

proposals.subtype: Obsolete alert-rule patch factory throwing unsupported
proposals.explanation: The hidden obsolete AlertRulePatch factory exposes tags, rule settings, condition, actions and update time but immediately throws NotSupportedException instead of creating a patch.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Its explicit unsupported implementation and public API annotations are supplied in handwritten compatibility code.

proposals.subtype: Obsolete data-container factory throwing unsupported
proposals.explanation: The hidden obsolete DataContainer factory retains a DataContainerWorkspace parameter and immediately throws NotSupportedException rather than wrapping that workspace.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The public factory's entire handwritten body is the explicit unsupported throw.

proposals.subtype: Obsolete data-container workspace factory throwing unsupported
proposals.explanation: The hidden obsolete DataContainerWorkspace factory retains ID, location and customer-ID arguments but immediately throws NotSupportedException instead of creating a result.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The non-generated compatibility factory explicitly implements this unsupported model-construction API.

proposals.subtype: Obsolete monitor-incident factory throwing unsupported
proposals.explanation: The public MonitorIncident factory retains name, rule name, activity and activation/resolution-time arguments but is hidden and obsolete and immediately throws NotSupportedException.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The explicit throwing method and metadata are handwritten outside Generated.

proposals.subtype: Obsolete private-link operation-status factory throwing unsupported
proposals.explanation: The hidden obsolete MonitorPrivateLinkScopeOperationStatus factory exposes its ID, name, times, status and error arguments but immediately throws NotSupportedException. Its operation-status result type and comments do not establish any handwritten polling implementation.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The supplied compatibility factory body directly implements an unsupported API rather than a generated poller.

proposals.subtype: Obsolete subscription-metric model factory throwing unsupported
proposals.explanation: The hidden obsolete SubscriptionMonitorMetric factory retains metric metadata, unit and time-series arguments but immediately throws NotSupportedException rather than producing a metric result.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: This complete unsupported public factory method is manually supplied in the compatibility partial.

proposals.subtype: Obsolete VM Insights onboarding-status factory throwing unsupported
proposals.explanation: The public VmInsightsOnboardingStatusData factory retains resource metadata, resource ID, onboarding/data statuses and data-container inputs but is hidden and obsolete and immediately throws NotSupportedException.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The complete throwing factory body and annotations are handwritten outside Generated.

proposals.subtype: Suppressed notification member replaced with clear-and-add list facade
proposals.explanation: The replacement Notifications property initializes missing AutoscaleSettingProperties in both accessors. Its getter returns the nested Notifications list; its setter clears that list before adding each supplied item when value is non-null, so null requests a clear. No input snapshot is taken before Clear, and the setter does not directly retain the input list reference.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: An active CodeGenSuppress and complete replacement property are coupled handwritten code in the compatibility partial.

proposals.subtype: Flattened association provisioned-by metadata
proposals.explanation: DataCollectionRuleAssociationData adds a get-only MetadataProvisionedBy string property directly returning Metadata?.ProvisionedBy without constructing a missing metadata object.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The computed property is manually implemented outside Generated in a compatibility model partial.

proposals.subtype: Association metadata string projected as ResourceIdentifier
proposals.explanation: MetadataProvisionedByResourceId returns null when Metadata or its ProvisionedByResourceId is null; otherwise it constructs a ResourceIdentifier from the nested value on access. No cached identifier or setter is supplied.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: This explicit typed projection is implemented in handwritten compatibility source outside Generated.

proposals.subtype: Flattened rule provisioned-by metadata
proposals.explanation: DataCollectionRuleData separately adds the get-only MetadataProvisionedBy string property returning Metadata?.ProvisionedBy. It is the same alias shape on a different model and does not initialize missing Metadata.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The complete getter is handwritten in this model's compatibility partial.

proposals.subtype: Rule metadata string projected as ResourceIdentifier
proposals.explanation: DataCollectionRuleData.MetadataProvisionedByResourceId null-checks the nested metadata resource-ID value and otherwise creates a ResourceIdentifier from it, providing a typed read-only projection rather than exposing the raw value.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The complete null-aware conversion getter is manually implemented outside Generated.

proposals.subtype: Cancellation-only list overloads supplying default paging arguments
proposals.explanation: The sync/async GetDataCollectionRuleAssociationsByRule overloads accept only cancellation and call their same-name overloads with named skipToken and top arguments set to default. This is omission/defaulting of paging parameters, not a custom page iterator or next-link algorithm; no obsolete/hidden annotation is present on these methods.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Both complete forwarding method expressions are supplied in non-generated compatibility source.

proposals.subtype: Delete overloads supplying a default association option
proposals.explanation: The sync/async Delete overloads accept WaitUntil and cancellation and forward both while supplying deleteAssociations: default to a same-name overload. The capture does not show that argument's type/default semantics or any operation implementation; returning ArmOperation does not establish a custom LRO wrapper or poller.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The two explicit forwarding expressions are handwritten outside Generated and form one defaulted-operation-option behavior.

decisions.reason: Lines 16-22 establish a handwritten TrackedResourceData declaration and location-forwarding constructor, but no generated base declaration is captured to demonstrate an override of a different base type. The proposed polymorphic-base-type-override pattern asserts a comparison the capture cannot make; classify the observable constructor shape instead.

finding.explanation: The handwritten ActivityLogAlertData partial declares TrackedResourceData as its base and supplies a public constructor taking AzureLocation and forwarding it to that base. The capture does not show a different generated base or establish the historical change described in its comments.
finding.handwrittenRationale: The explicit base declaration and location constructor occur in src/Customization/Compatibility, outside Generated.

decisions.reason: Lines 27-45 implement a public ConditionAllOf facade over Properties, allocate the properties bag when absent, and set a new AlertRuleAllOfCondition rather than assigning the getter's list; the model-property-alias shape and model category match the handwritten partial.

The non-generated AlertRuleCollection at lines 16-89 is hidden, obsolete, and uniformly throws in its operations and enumeration; its protected constructor is for mocking. This is a retired compatibility facade, not a functioning pager, existence helper, or custom LRO.

Lines 18-64 retain a hidden obsolete model's properties and constructor/interface signatures while construction and JSON/persistence methods throw, except the literal format result. Model surface compatibility is supported, not a working serializer; the supplied pattern describes the shim.

Lines 19-160 show a hidden obsolete resource with ResourceType, non-throwing uninitialized Data/HasData auto-properties, and throwing service/serialization members. The one retired resource facade is handwritten; neither ArmOperation signatures nor pageable signatures implement custom polling or paging.

The suppression at line 17 and obsolete overload at lines 35-63 show an actual legacy factory adapter: it converts supported aggregation values when non-null, converts the primary argument through the helper, and forwards. The unseen helper and destination bodies are not asserted; legacy-overload-compatibility is apt.

Lines 70-74 preserve the obsolete public AlertRuleData model-factory signature with a throwing body. Model overrides describes the retained factory API shape, not working construction; backward-compatibility-shim captures its handwritten unsupported behavior.

Lines 81-84 retain a hidden obsolete DiagnosticSettingsCategoryData factory accepting metadata and category arguments but unconditionally throwing. This is a model-factory API compatibility stub, not a constructed output model.

Lines 91-94 show the handwritten obsolete DiagnosticSettingData factory and immediate unsupported exception; the many destination parameters do not imply any destination dispatch or wire conversion. The model-factory compatibility shape is accurately identified.

Lines 101-104 retain an obsolete AlertRulePatch factory signature and immediately throw. This is handwritten retention of a model/patch factory API, not actual patch creation, and the proposed shim pattern fits.
Lines 111-114 define an obsolete DataContainer factory with a DataContainerWorkspace argument and an unconditional throw; the retained factory API is handwritten but performs no wrapping.

Lines 121-124 retain the obsolete DataContainerWorkspace factory's ID/location/customer-ID signature and an immediate throw. This is a distinct public model-factory compatibility stub, not working construction.
Lines 131-134 retain an obsolete MonitorIncident factory with its incident/time parameters and an unconditional throw. The handwritten model-factory API shim is distinct from any incident operation.

Lines 141-144 retain an obsolete MonitorPrivateLinkScopeOperationStatus factory and throw immediately; its operation-status return type is not evidence of a custom poller or operation-status extraction.

Lines 151-154 retain the obsolete SubscriptionMonitorMetric factory with metric/unit/time-series parameters but unconditionally throw. No metric model is created or serialized by this handwritten stub.

Lines 161-164 retain the obsolete VmInsightsOnboardingStatusData factory's resource/status/data arguments but immediately throw. This distinct handwritten model-factory compatibility stub does not build an onboarding result.

Lines 12-40 suppress Notifications and replace it with a property that creates Properties on demand, returns its nested list, and clears then re-adds setter input. This is not a property alias/addition: the same-name property's setter explicitly mutates a nested collection. The catalog has no exact replacement-and-mutation shape.

finding.subtype: Suppressed notification member replaced with clear-and-add list facade
finding.explanation: A handwritten Notifications property replaces the suppressed member: both accessors create AutoscaleSettingProperties when absent, the getter returns its nested list, and the setter clears that list and adds each supplied item when non-null. Passing null clears the list; no input snapshot precedes clearing, so self-assignment of the returned list can clear it.
finding.handwrittenRationale: CodeGenSuppress and the replacement getter/setter occur in src/Customization/Compatibility outside Generated.

decisions.reason: The handwritten association-data property at line 13 directly projects Metadata?.ProvisionedBy as a nullable string without initialization; the model-property-alias classification matches this flattening.
Line 16 in the association model null-checks the nested metadata ID and constructs a ResourceIdentifier on access; this separate read-only typed projection has no shown cache or setter.
Line 13 in DataCollectionRuleData implements its own Metadata?.ProvisionedBy string alias. It is a distinct model-member instance from the identical shape on the association model.
Line 16 in DataCollectionRuleData returns null for missing nested metadata ID and otherwise constructs ResourceIdentifier; this is a distinct handwritten typed-property projection on another model.

Lines 21-30 implement sync and async cancellation-only list overloads supplying default skipToken and top arguments. Pagination captures paging-parameter API shaping, not a custom iterator or next-link algorithm; page-size-option-alias describes the shared shape.

Lines 38-48 implement sync and async Delete overloads forwarding WaitUntil/cancellation and a default deleteAssociations argument. The fixed-argument helper pattern fits; ArmOperation return types alone establish no handwritten polling.

limitations: Coverage is partial: all nine complete captured source texts and all three complete generation contexts were read, but only 9 of 856 eligible files among 912 discovered files are captured. All 77 skipped inventory entries were read only as coverage metadata, not as evidence of their uncaptured implementations.

No generated counterpart, helper implementation, referenced specification, SDK history, uncaptured compatibility type or other URL was independently inspected. Comments asserting prior API shapes, generator behavior, removed specification models or service requirements are not verified causes.

The uniformly retired AlertRule collection/model/resource facades are each grouped by their single compatibility-placeholder behavior, including their unsupported operations or codec interfaces, rather than counting every identical throw as implemented paging, LRO, tagging or serialization logic. The surviving factory partial's ten distinct retired output-model factory APIs are separate instances.

The two resource-data metadata properties on each model are distinct string aliases and typed identifier projections. Matching shapes on different model types remain distinct instances; no ResourceIdentifier constructor internals are supplied.

The metric-definition overload invokes an uncaptured aggregation conversion helper and uncaptured factory destination; exact enum mappings, destination behavior and historical compatibility are not inferred.

ActivityLogAlertData's explicit base clause and constructor are observed contract customizations, but a change from a generated proxy base is unproven without the generated counterpart. The nested alert-condition and autoscale-model constructors and serializers are also unavailable.

Notifications clears its target list before enumerating value and takes no snapshot first; no safe self-assignment, collection immutability or deep copy is claimed. Getter/setter initialization and suppression are coupled parts of one property finding.

The cancellation-only association-list and delete overloads are not annotated obsolete or hidden. They supply named default arguments without establishing legacy necessity, actual paging behavior or custom polling. Generator-addressable judgments are plausible generic structural opportunities, not measured current capabilities.

Only nine source files of 856 eligible files were captured, with 77 explicitly skipped source paths; skipped inventory names are not source bodies. The captured files support neither an exhaustive customization count nor any absence claim.

The three generation-context captures identify the package and TypeSpec location but do not include generated counterparts, old releases, helper implementations, or actual generator behavior. Historical explanations in source comments and claims about current generator capability remain unverified; generatorAddressable describes only plausible generalizability.

The retired AlertRule operation methods and obsolete unsupported factory stubs throw, but the model/resource format getters return the literal J; AlertRuleResource Data/HasData are non-throwing uninitialized properties, and the distinct legacy MonitorMetricDefinition factory adapter forwards after conversion. Unsupported signatures must not be interpreted as functioning paging, serialization, polling or service operations. Acceptance denotes AI review only, not human verification.
